original_value: CODING DECISION: Art. 10 is fundamentally a data governance provision, even though some of its requirements relate to risk mitigation. It is coded under Risk Assessment for now because its core operative elements, bias examination (Art. 10(2)(f)), bias detection, prevention and mitigation (Art. 10(2)(g)) and identification of data gaps (Art. 10(2)(h)), are risk identification and mitigation functions. Secondary dimension: Data Governance (see secondary_dimension; candidate sixth dimension for the codebook). A further link to Safety and Testing (quality of testing data sets) is noted but not coded. Single record, no double count. AMENDMENT: Reg. (EU) 2026/1744 amended Art. 10(1) (M1 marker) so the quality criteria now refer to paras 2, 3 and 4 and to Art. 4a(1) instead of paras 2 to 5. It also deleted Art. 10(5) and moved the special-category data rule into new Art. 4a (cons. p. 12). The coded exact_text (opening of Art. 10(2)) appears unamended. PERMISSION vs OBLIGATION: Art. 4a(1) PERMITS providers of high-risk AI systems, exceptionally and where strictly necessary, to process special categories of personal data for the bias detection and correction required by Art. 10(2)(f)-(g), subject to cumulative safeguards. Art. 4a(2) extends that permission to providers and deployers of other AI systems and models and to deployers of high-risk systems, and expressly states that it does not create any obligation to conduct bias detection and correction. So the DUTY to examine and mitigate bias comes from Art. 10(2)(f)-(g) and binds high-risk providers only, while Art. 4a is an enabling permission, not an obligation, and is not coded as a separate mandatory record. Must be read alongside the GDPR (Art. 1(2)(g) as amended is without prejudice to Art. 4a). APPLICATION DATE: as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744, Art. 113 (cons. p. 128; OJ p. 123) applies Chapter III high-risk obligations from 2 Dec 2027 for systems classified under Art. 6(2) and Annex III, and from 2 Aug 2028 for systems classified under Art. 6(1) and Annex I (originally 2 Aug 2026 and 2 Aug 2027 respectively). As of Nov 2026 the obligation is binding law but not yet applicable. original_value: High-risk AI systems must be designed so that natural persons can effectively oversee them while in use, with the aim of preventing or minimising risks to health, safety or fundamental rights. Oversight measures must be proportionate to risk, autonomy and context, and may be built in by the provider or identified by the provider for the deployer to implement. The system must be provided to the deployer so that the people assigned to oversight are enabled, as appropriate and proportionate, to understand its capacities and limitations, remain aware of automation bias, interpret its outputs, decide not to use or to override an output, and stop the system safely (Art. 14(4)).
